newsitem.title: UK: Good margins continue to lift Med/W Africa crudes.
newsitem.headline: Good margins continue to lift Med/W Africa crudes.

text.p: Mediterranean and West African crudes held steady to firmer on Wednesday as good refining margins from gas oil and high sulphur fuel oil continued, traders said.
As a result Urals was talked somewhat firmer around dated Brent -$1.10-$1.00 a barrel cif and was not yet affected by cheaper May Iraqi Kirkuk crude.

Talk of a May loading cargo of Iraqi Kirkuk selling this week at Dated Brent -$1.30 cif Augusta could not be confirmed but traders saw this as market level. This would mean the grade was selling at the equivalent of OSP +30-40 cents.
"And that is still cheap relative to Urals," one Kirkuk lifter said.
Up to further two cargoes of May-loading Kirkuk were heard offered on the spot market.

The cut in April in the number of companies allowed to export Urals through the export programme was not affecting exports through Novorossiisk as other exporters had increased their volumes, traders said.
If April exports for the remainder of the month continued at their current rate they will be the highest for six months.
Urals' prices should hold for the next three weeks or so, traders said and the planned maintenance on Berth Two at Novorossiisk for 22-23 days from May 6 should help support differentials.
"I'm bullish over the short term and bearish in the long term," one refiner said.

"There are good margins especially on high sulphur fuel oil but refiners are running at full capacity and that will flood the market at some stage soon. My impression is the market will come off in three weeks time unless outright prices rise and Iraqi exports have to drop off," he added.
Some West African crude traders said they expected the Uruguayan state oil refiner ANCAP to chose Angolan or West African crudes to fill their one million barrels buy tender which closes on April 28.
The awards will be made on April 29. ANCAP has taken Gulf of Suez crude in the last two tenders.
Venezuela's Lagoven buy tender for 500,000 barrels of May 25-27 arrival Syrian or Urals crude will close on Thursday, traders said.
A trading company was head to have sold a May 25-27 cargo of Qua Iboe to a Spanish refiner on Tuesday at Dated Brent +41 cents, reflecting the recent rise in West African differentials.
As good buying interest continued into the U.S. and Asia in particular, grades were expected to hold their own over the next few weeks.
